chunks: Any believer who washes a believer and says, when turning him: “O Allah, this is the body of Your believing servant, and You have taken his soul from him and separated the two of them, so Your pardon, Your pardon, Your pardon,” Allah will forgive the sins of a year, except the major sins.

key_terms.الْكَبَائِرَ: major sins, which are excluded from the promised forgiveness
key_terms.بَدَنُ: the physical body of the deceased servant
key_terms.ذُنُوبَ: sins that are forgiven as a result of this act
key_terms.رُوحَهُ: his soul, which Allah has taken from the body
key_terms.عَفْوَكَ: Your pardon; a plea for Allah’s forgiveness and overlooking of faults
key_terms.غَسَّلَ: washed the dead body in the prescribed ritual manner
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer; here, both the deceased and the one performing the washing

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited while washing the body of a deceased believer?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited while washing the deceased believer, expressing awareness that Allah has separated the soul from the body. It also conveys the great merit of serving the deceased with this du'a, as Allah forgives a year's sins for the one who performs it, apart from major sins.
